questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

I will be study around 7 o’clock.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect verb form "**be study**."
 
• The correct verb form should be "**be studying**" to indicate the continuous tense.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**I will be studying around 7 o'clock**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I will be studying around 7 o'clock."*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She were singing / beautifully in / the concert hall / last night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the plural form of the verb 'were' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the subject **'She'** is **singular** and should be followed by the **singular form of the verb** '**was**'.
 
• The correct sentence should use the **singular form** of the verb to match the singular subject.
 
• Therefore, the singular form of the verb 'was' should be used in place of the plural form 'were'.

Correct sentence: *She **was singing** beautifully in the concert hall last night.*

questions.question:
Identify the error in the following sentence and select the option with the correct use of the phrasal verb.

The police inspector was trying to give out the contradicting stories in the scene of the accident.

options.text: The police inspector was trying to lighten up the contradicting stories in the scene of the accident.
The police inspector was trying to rush out the contradicting stories in the scene of the accident.
The police inspector was trying to sign up the contradicting stories in the scene of the accident.
The police inspector was trying to sort out the contradicting stories in the scene of the accident.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the 4th sentence, the correct phrasal verb should be "**sort out**" which means to organize or resolve something.
 
• The phrase "**sort out the contradicting stories**" makes sense in the context of the police inspector trying to resolve or make sense of the conflicting information.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The police inspector was trying to sort out the contradicting stories in the scene of the accident."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "lighten up" means to make something less serious, which is not suitable in this context.
 
• **Option 2:** "rush out" means to produce something quickly, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 3:** "sign up" means to register or enlist, which is irrelevant here.

• **Example: **The opacity of the frosted glass ensured privacy in the room.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'transparency' **is **'opacity'**.
